The covering follows the body outline. Declared fiction: arthropod parts at large size, shown with thick supporting legs and visible breathing openings along the flanks. Bilaterally symmetrical, recognizable limbs, visible sense organs. Habitat cue (forest): dark back and light belly (mild countershading). Prosaic detail: natural lighting, feet in firm contact with the ground with a soft shadow, normal wear on hooves, claws and skin. One creature, full body, side three-quarter view, plain light background, natural history illustration.

spark_open.description: The creature is a quadrupedal animal with the overall body shape, dense shaggy fur, head, limbs and tail of a brown bear combined with the dorsal exoskeleton and frontal horn of a rhinoceros beetle. It stands in right-facing profile against a plain light background, covered in thick brown fur that is darker on the legs and lower body and lighter tan on the muzzle, with a bear-like head, small rounded ears, four sturdy legs ending in clawed paws, and a very small furry tail at the rear. Its back and shoulders are covered by a large, highly glossy dark reddish-brown to black chitinous structure, and a single large curved glossy horn with a forward-pointing tine projects upward and backward from its forehead.

meta_spark.description: A large four-legged mammal with the thick shaggy brown fur, stocky build, head shape, ears, paws and claws of a brown bear, shown in side profile facing right. Fused to its back is a glossy dark reddish-brown beetle carapace with ribbed elytra covering the mid-back to rump and a smooth domed pronotum shield over the shoulders, with a row of small round breathing holes visible in the fur just below the shell edge. A single long curved glossy dark beetle horn with a small forward-pointing tine rises from the center of its forehead between the bear ears.
